source.section: PDF page 7, Line 20 (interest income on state and local bonds and obligations of other states); Form IT-201 line 20; Form IT-201 lines 19, 24, 32-39 (PDF pages 2-3); IT-201-I PDF page 11 (line 34 standard deduction table), PDF pages 12 and 33 (line 39, rate schedule)

worked: Single, 50, wages 80,000; tax-exempt interest 3,000 from New York State and local bonds and 2,000 from another state's bonds (neither in federal AGI). Federal AGI (IT-201 line 19) = 80,000.00. Federal taxable income = 80,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 64,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Addition: line 20 interest on other states' bonds (New York bonds 3,000 not added) 2,000.00. Line 24 = 80,000.00 + 2,000.00 = 82,000.00. Line 32 total subtractions = 0.00. Line 33 New York AGI = 82,000.00 - 0.00 = 82,000.00. Line 34 New York standard deduction (single, PDF page 11 table) 8,000.00; line 35 = 82,000.00 - 8,000.00 = 74,000.00; line 36 dependent exemption 0 (no dependents); lines 37/38 taxable income 74,000.00. Rate schedule (PDF page 33, single) on 74,000.00: 8,500.00 x 4% = 340.00; 3,200.00 x 4.5% = 144.00; 2,200.00 x 5.25% = 115.50; 60,100.00 x 5.5% = 3,305.50; schedule tax = 3,905.00 (the printed schedule, with its whole-dollar base 600 at 13,900, gives 3,905.50; this case uses the bands as numbers). NY AGI is 107,650 or less and line 38 is 65,000 or more: the rate schedule applies (PDF page 12, line 39); no recapture worksheet. Line 39 NYS tax = 3,905.00. Credits: none (the household credit, line 40, PDF page 12 tables 1-3, allows no credit above federal AGI of 28,000 single or 32,000 other statuses): state income tax = 3,905.00.
